answer: In a harbor market where AI agents trade saffron, each agent must lock a bond for 30 days, and its trading quota is proportional to that bond. Creating a thousand identities gives an attacker no more total quota than putting the same funds behind one agent, because each bond can back only one account at a time. The market offers no haven for free identities: scaling an attack requires tying up proportionally more capital and losing its use elsewhere.
